failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'Who was Ion Țiriac's men's doubles partner when he won the 1970 French Open, and is this person a Christian minister who also won a singles title with Jan Kodes and currently resides in Australia?' Hop 3 query: 'Who won the 1970 French Open men's singles title and men's doubles title with Ion Țiriac, did they win a doubles title with Jan Kodeš, are they a Christian minister, and do they currently reside in Australia?' Both queries are natural-language yes/no questions bundling multiple targets (partner identity, minister status, Kodes connection, residence) into compound multi-part asks.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query asks 'Who was Ion Țiriac's men's doubles partner when he won the 1970 French Open, and is this person a Christian minister who also won a singles title with Jan Kodes and currently resides in Australia?' Hop 3 query asks 'Who won the 1970 French Open men's singles title and men's doubles title with Ion Țiriac, did they win a doubles title with Jan Kodeš, are they a Christian minister, and do they currently reside in Australia?' The queries re-ask the same core questions (Țiriac's partner, minister status, Kodes connection, Australia residence) with only minor rephrasing, failing to advance based on retrieved information.

failure_modes.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
failure_modes.evidence: Summary 1 explicitly names the missing evidence: '1970 French Open tournament results (singles and men's doubles)' and 'Information about Jan Kodes and his tennis partnerships'. Hop 2 query targets this with 'Who was Ion Țiriac's men's doubles partner when he won the 1970 French Open' and 'won a singles title with Jan Kodes'. Hop 3 query similarly asks 'Who won the 1970 French Open men's singles title and men's doubles title with Ion Țiriac, did they win a doubles title with Jan Kodeš'. Despite well-formed targeting of the gap, retrieved passages include badminton players (Kojima, McCoig, Rattanusorn) and tennis players from different years (1971 French Open, 1996 French Open) but never the 1970 French Open doubles partner or results.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: Solver summaries repeatedly process passages about badminton players (Ippei Kojima appears in multiple retrieval hops, plus Sangob Rattanusorn and Robert S. McCoig) despite the claim being exclusively about tennis Grand Slam titles. These badminton passages are clearly irrelevant to verifying a claim about the French Open and tennis partnerships.
